For eligible negative set E, M=|E|≥32 and 32 uniform draws without replacement, inclusion probability π=32/M. Uncorrected sampled CE is L=−s⁺+log(exp(s⁺)+Σ exp(sⱼ)). A partition-estimation correction gives L̂=−s⁺+log(exp(s⁺)+(M/32)Σ exp(sⱼ)): implement CE on [s⁺, s⁻−log(32/M)], leaving the guaranteed positive unchanged. This estimates the partition over {positive}∪E; finite-sample loss/gradients remain biased. Applying the same uniform correction to every logit cancels and yields uncorrected CE. Specify the convention explicitly. [Candidate-sampling definitions](https://www.tensorflow.org/extras/candidate_sampling.pdf), [positive-inclusion distinction](https://arxiv.org/html/2507.09331v1).

gSASRec instead uses L=[β·softplus(−s⁺)+Σ softplus(sⱼ)]/33, β=1−t+tα, originally α=32/(|I|−1). Thus t=0 gives BCE; t=1 gives β=α. This changes positive weighting, without softmax competition or logQ subtraction. For a restricted eligible population, α=32/M is the corresponding inclusion-rate adaptation, not the published global-catalog implementation; history-dependent exclusion does not automatically inherit its calibration theorem. Both score 33 items/position: O(BL·33d), with similar scoring cost; the official implementation additionally uses float64 positive-logit conversion, avoidable with the direct softplus expression. [Equations and implementation](https://github.com/asash/gsasrec).

Original SASRec explicitly excludes `set(user_train[user])` at every position: full training-history exclusion, including later training interactions. Causal-prefix exclusion instead constructs Eₜ=I\(set(history≤t)∪{targetₜ}); later interactions remain eligible. These produce different M values and negative semantics. Implement distinct draws using `choice(eligible,32,replace=False)`; if M<32, reduce k and update corrections/normalization. The official gSASRec PyTorch sampler uses unrestricted `torch.randint`: duplicates and history/target collisions are possible, so it implements neither exclusion policy. [Original sampler](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/kang205/SASRec/master/sampler.py), [gSASRec sampler](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/asash/gSASRec-pytorch/main/dataset_utils.py).
